cim: UVA President Scott Beardsley charts University’s future in artificial intelligence
cim_eredeti: UVA President Scott Beardsley charts University’s future in artificial intelligence
szoveg_eredeti:
President Scott Beardsley says UVA will harness the potential of artificial intelligence across the University while prioritizing responsible use and human judgment. (Photo by Lathan Goumas, University Communications)

On Friday, UVA President Scott Beardsley sent an email to the University community outlining his vision for the role artificial intelligence will play at UVA. His note is below:

To the University community:Few technologies have changed how people live, learn, work, and communicate as quickly as artificial intelligence. Though AI has been around for decades and has been part of the development of the internet, social media, and broadband communications, the emergence of agentic AI is accelerating the pace of transformation and sparking discussions across university campuses, including our own. At the University of Virginia, we are meeting this moment with purpose and conviction.UVA was founded on the belief that education should serve the public good – especially in moments of rapid and profound change. With that purpose in mind, our scholars and stakeholders have been advancing the understanding of AI for years and confronting the hard questions it raises for society. We have backed that purpose with sustained investment in AI, spanning research, institutes, infrastructure, and partnerships with leading companies. And we are leading important discussions. Just this week, I joined colleagues in the Contemplative Sciences Center for a fascinating symposium on AI and Human Flourishing, and the LaCross Institute for Ethical AI in Business at the Darden School of Business will soon host a conference.While we cannot fully understand how AI will shape the future, this memo offers guideposts aligned with our mission and values in developing, applying, and understanding AI.

Beardsley says UVA is preparing students for an AI-driven workforce, adapting curricula, expanding career services and building industry partnerships. He participated in the Contemplative Sciences Center’s recent AI Anxiety + Human Flourishing symposium. (Photo by Lathan Goumas, University Communications)

At UVA, we will approach AI with ambition and principle. We will leverage AI technologies where they can enhance our work, productivity, and mission. We will support our innovators as they advance the technologies and develop new uses for them. We will consider critically AI’s impact on humanity, education, and society. We will interpret this unique moment and chart a way forward that is consistent with Thomas Jefferson’s founding vision for the University to develop citizen leaders and serve the public good.What this means in practice is that:We will lead. For more than three decades, UVA researchers have advanced AI and large language models. That work continues today. UVA offers more than 100 AI-focused courses per year and is hiring and developing faculty with a wide array of AI expertise. AI instruction is embedded in all 12 schools. We are investing in the needed computing power through the new Fontaine Computing and Innovation Center and spearheading the Commonwealth AI Initiative that unites universities, industry, government, and nonprofits to establish Virginia as a source of trusted, responsible AI expertise.We will promote ethical applications for the good of society. We will study with rigor AI’s effects on society, the environment, democracy, work, and well-being. UVA will help shape and debate not only what AI can do, but what it should do and how to achieve these goals through policy, regulation, and legislation. This work takes place every day across disciplines and schools, including the first data science school in the country, and at the LaCross Institute.We will prioritize human judgment. At UVA, we will not outsource consequential decisions to machines. In our classrooms, labs, clinics, and offices, AI will support human judgment – not replace it.We will teach students to think, not just prompt. Our goal is to develop graduates who have technical literacy in AI but can also question it, critically interpret it, and know when to set it aside. I believe the most successful universities will pair the newest technologies with the oldest methods of teaching and learning: the Socratic seminar, the blue book, oral exams, the argument defended aloud. Our graduates will use AI to sharpen their thinking – not replace it. We will provide equitable access to secure tools. In the Academic Division, UVA’s Information Technology Services already offers embedded AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot Chat and Google Gemini. However, many in the community are paying for licenses to additional tools. We are committed to providing equitable access and exploring frontier AI platforms where we can learn and experiment together. We will share more information soon.We will prepare our students for a changing workplace. AI is shaping nearly every profession and is a trillion-dollar industry. Our graduates are entering a job market that is different from that of previous generations. We will walk with our students on this journey. We are building an infrastructure to track AI’s effects on the workplace in partnership with employers, recruiters, and alumni. Based on our learnings, we will continue to adapt our curricula to prepare students to succeed in the workplace. We will bolster our career services to help students translate their education into meaningful work or ongoing study, and we will partner with AI-related companies to hire our students and collaborate with our faculty on research. Equally, we will promote and facilitate entrepreneurial innovation in the application of AI.We will protect the relationships at the heart of a UVA education. Jefferson founded this University on the belief that people learn best through genuine human relationships built on discussion and debate. We have some of the most beautiful Grounds in the world, which foster human connection. Technology will not diminish that conviction and connection. A faculty member or fellow student who pushes others to think harder or consider a different viewpoint is core to the value of a UVA education.We will protect academic freedom and Honor. Faculty will continue to decide what resources students may use in completing their coursework and the technologies permitted in their classrooms. Whether they embrace AI, restrict it, or take a hybrid approach, faculty must be clear about their expectations. Our students are bound by the Honor Code, our community’s foundation of trust. In our proud tradition of student self-governance, students are leading the discussion on upholding Honor in the age of AI. We will act on what we learn. Four standing University committees on AI – for teaching and learning, research, operations, and policy and use – will advise us as this work unfolds. We will act on what we learn, and we will keep listening.We will invest in and use AI responsibly to advance our mission. Just as we invested in earlier generations of computing, we will pilot AI with care across our operations to drive innovation in service of our mission of education, research, patient care, and public service.We will be agile and adaptive. No one has a crystal ball. We will continuously reassess and adapt as the technology advances at exponential rates.In the coming weeks, interim Provost Brie Gertler will share updates on AI applications in the Academic Division, and Dr. Mitch Rosner will share updates with UVA Health. Learn more at AI@UVA, and listen to the faculty-led AI Exchange@UVA podcast for an interview with me and others.As we ambitiously advance the science and scholarship of AI, we will cultivate the human capacity to use it wisely. And we will remember, in every classroom, lab, and hospital room, that human judgment and relationships are core to our success. Sincerely,

Scott C. BeardsleyPresident, University of Virginia
